# Relative sizes in table cells

These are original OPC/XML and PNG controls generated by
`tools/table_relative_anchors_fixture.py`, using the original table-anchor
controls as a base. There are 22 pages each for compatibility modes 15 and 12.
The four repeating cases request page 25% width / 10% height, margin 25% / 10%,
page 25% width / inactive height, and inactive width / margin 10% height.
They cross stacking, layoutInCell, offsets, alignment, padding and exact rows.

The reference application exported each PDF after its exact source path was
confirmed. `tools/record_table_global_anchors.py --relative` (plus `--legacy`)
records source/PDF hashes, PDF image matrices, cell bounds and visible blue ink.
The expected frames come from the reference application, not our layout implementation.

The size bases remain the physical page/writing area, while placement follows
the existing cell-coordinate rules. Standalone pictures fit proportionally into
the requested box, even without an aspect-lock declaration. For example, a
72 by 36 pt picture requested at 99 by 57.6 pt paints at 99 by 49.5 pt.
Zero metadata retains the corresponding saved dimension. Alignment uses the
requested box before the proportional fit, including legacy page centering.
These observations refine the MS-ODRAWXML relative-size behavior; no new conflict
with a normative rule was identified. Previously documented mode-15 cell-anchor
compatibility differences continue to apply.

The complementary four-page `relative-body-anchors` control proves this picture
rule outside tables. `relative-group-anchors` instead groups the same picture;
The reference application scales each group axis independently (99 by 57.6 pt in the example).
`tools/relative_anchor_kind_fixture.py` generates both. All group drawings are
foreground so each complete frame can be compared without cell-fill occlusion.

Browser checks compare all page ink bounds, then edit adjacent text, export,
reopen and undo exactly. Unit checks compare native reference frames, hit testing, selection
and package preservation. These certify the tested drawing behavior, not full
OOXML layout or arbitrary scene text/stroke scaling.
